# An OMOP-Based Open-Source Text-to-SQL Benchmark Dataset

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#text-to-omop)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2026.clinicalnlp-1.40.pdf) · ClinicalNLP at LREC 2026 proceedings, printed pages 381–393

**Reading coverage:** All 13 pages including sections 1–9, all five tables, construction/split diagrams, prompts and concrete examples in supplementary section 8.

## Research question

Evaluate OMOP-grounded SQL generation and abstention while separating concept identification from SQL reasoning.

## Method

The dataset adapts EHRSQL templates, supplies typed concept/person identifiers and pairs supported SQL with exact `<NO_SQL>` refusals. LoRA tuning is evaluated on a synthetic PostgreSQL OMOP instance populated to make gold queries non-empty.

## Evaluation

The test mixes seen SQL variations and held-out variations. Section 8.2 specifies 745 answerable test paraphrases from variations also represented in training plus 185 from unseen variations, with 232 negatives. Execution scoring ignores row/column order and maps NULL to empty strings; a stricter column comparison is also reported.

## What the results support

The adapted checkpoint strongly outperforms schema-injected baselines under this contract. Two LoRA checkpoints are from one training run, not independent methods. Remaining failures include visit hierarchy, event-table choice and unsupported normative questions.

## Limits and qualifications

The statement that paraphrases of a query never cross splits conflicts with the explicit 20/5/5 seen-variation allocation. Results therefore do not represent wholly unseen-template or SQL-structure generalization. Inputs already contain identifiers, the database is synthetic and OMOP constraints are not enforced.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A bounded clinical SQL-or-refuse benchmark; retain concept-normalization, mixed seen/unseen evaluation and synthetic-data limits.
